newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks down,dollar climbs on Yen worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks down,dollar climbs on Yen worries.

text.p: London and Frankfurt stocks fell sharply in quiet early trade on Friday with much of Europe closed for a public holiday and with Wall Street's unimpressive finish failing to provide direction.

In currency markets, the dollar showed a little life and climbed half a yen as concern grew that the slide of many SouthEast Asian currencies would hurt the Japanese economy. Sterling was stronger against the mark and dollar.

London and Frankfurt were two of the only bourses operating on the Assumption Day holiday and their negative start followed a patchy performance on Thursday despite widespread relief that U.S. July consumer prices showed little threat to the bull markets on both sides of the Atlantic.
"Looks like a bit of a dull start to a dull day. It's going to be dead," a London dealer said as the blue-chip FTSE 100 index slipped 0.7 percent to 4,955.6 points at one stage.
Among shares weighing on the market was satellite TV broadcaster BSkyB, which fell 15 pence to 455 after profits failed to meet expectations.

In Frankfurt, stocks fell 1.4 percent in low-volume floor trade that tracked losses in post-bourse dealings on Thursday. The 30-share DAX index was down 59.76 points, at 4,171.67 points by mid-morning.

In currencies, trade was quiet in a market that was characterised by the weaker yen. The Japanese currency fell against the mark and sterling, and was down to 118.40 yen to the dollar, compared to 117.85 in late dealings on Thursday.

The benchmark Japanese bond yield fell to a record low of 2.065 percent overnight. Analysts said the yen, once the safe-haven currency of Asia, has finally fallen victim to the currency crisis sweeping the region.

Traders said that given the magnitude of the economic and financial ties between Japan and other Asian nations and the poor investment climate in Japan, continued turmoil in Asia is likely to trigger yen sales against the U.S. dollar.

On Thursday Indonesia's central bank said it was lifting the intervention band with immediate effect, virtually making the rupiah a freely floating currency -- the latest among Asian nations since Thailand's similar announcement on July 2.
"The yen's weakness is due to more than just one factor but it is hard to see anything positive for the yen out of the Asian currency crisis," said Kit Juckes, currency strategist at NatWest Markets.
"About half of Japan's trade is within Asia, so its losing some of its competitive edge there, even though Hong Kong and China are more important for Japan," Juckes said.
The dollar was unchanged against the mark although speculation about a German rate rise is likely to intensify in the run-up to next week's Bundesbank council meeting, analysts said.
"This should tend to keep the mark relatively well supported through the early part of the week," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.

Comments late on Thursday by Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum that the central bank was concerned about signs of continued consumer price inflation and that it wanted leeway on the repo rate had little net impact.

Sterling was also up against the mark and dollar in early Europe compared with late Thursday's European levels, though traders said the pound was still vulnerable to market worries over a possible rise in German interest rates.
The pound was at 2.9440 marks against Thursday's late European level of 2.9300 and against the dollar was at $1.5996 from $1.5872.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.8407 marks and 118.40 yen, compared with 1.8417 and 117.85 in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 32.7 points at 4,958.6.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 55.94 points at 4,175.59.
PARIS - Closed.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $323.50 an ounce , compared to Thursday's close of $326.25. Silver was down eight cents at $4.42.
